strengths: Vid2World addresses an important problem: adapting pretrained video generators for autoregressive, action-conditioned simulation. The combination of causal architecture changes, Diffusion Forcing, and action guidance is practical and clearly motivated.

The CS:GO results show substantial short-horizon improvements over DIAMOND-HQ: FVD decreases from 562.2 to 102.6 and LPIPS from 0.510 to 0.407. The qualitative comparisons also show improved sharpness and action responsiveness.
The mixed weight transfer ablation provides useful evidence for the initialization strategy: RT-1 FVD improves from 27.9 to 22.1 and PSNR from 21.9 to 23.9 under the reported training budget.

Evaluation covers both robot manipulation and gaming, including a closed-loop policy-evaluation demonstration. The appendix supplies substantial implementation details and candid examples of failures involving grasping and object identity.
weaknesses: The methodological novelty is limited relative to Diffusion Forcing, causal masking, framewise conditioning, and standard classifier-free guidance. Moreover, the claim that bidirectional denoisers are fundamentally incompatible with autoregressive prediction is overstated: generating the next frame using only available history does not inherently require a causal internal architecture. A pretrained, noncausal Diffusion Forcing baseline would help establish the benefit of architectural causalization.

Evidence for reliable action-conditioned dynamics is substantially weaker than evidence for visual quality. Most quantitative evaluation concerns 16-frame clips, with only 12 predicted frames in CS:GO. Figure 11 demonstrates qualitative responsiveness but does not establish counterfactual accuracy. Quantitative action-following tests, comparisons against actual outcomes under alternative actions, and longer-horizon error measurements are missing.

The downstream policy-evaluation claim is not convincingly supported. Figure 4 assigns RT-1 (Begin) 34.1% simulated success despite 0% real-world success, demonstrating substantial miscalibration. Preserving the ordering of three checkpoints from one policy family on one drawer-closing task is limited evidence. The experiment uses 80 rollouts per policy without confidence intervals, evaluator-agreement statistics, or a competing simulator baseline.

The comparisons do not sufficiently establish superiority over existing transfer methods. Table 1 imports baselines from AVID but omits AVID itself, and its baseline FID values are explicitly acknowledged to be incorrect without being recomputed. Autoregressive Vid2World improves RT-1 FVD over action-conditioned fine-tuning but worsens SSIM, LPIPS, and PSNR. The CS:GO comparison also leaves the effects of pretraining, native resolution, available history, and inference compute entangled with the proposed adaptation method.

The ablations incompletely isolate the proposed contributions. Removing action guidance also removes action dropout during training, confounding training regularization with inference guidance. Mixed weight transfer is compared only against shifted initialization, without aligned zero or random initialization controls. Ablations use only RT-1 and 30k training steps, while headline results use 100k; no uncertainty estimates establish the robustness of the smaller gains.

The broad claims about generality, scalability, and practical interactivity exceed the demonstrated scope. Only one pretrained U-Net backbone is evaluated, with no data-efficiency study or transfer to unseen environments. Sampling requires 50 DDIM steps per generated frame with guidance, but latency, throughput, memory use, and quality versus inference-cost comparisons are absent. These omissions matter for the proposed interactive game-engine application.

The CS:GO improvements are substantial: FVD decreases from 368.5 for DIAMOND-HQ to 106.6, and FID from 87.2 to 17.5. Robot prediction also improves FVD over action-conditioned fine-tuning, from 24.2 to 18.5.

The manuscript includes component ablations, a closed-loop policy-evaluation demonstration, detailed implementation settings, and informative failure cases. These provide useful evidence beyond selected successful generations.
weaknesses: The methodological novelty is narrower than the framing suggests. Diffusion Forcing, causal attention masks, frame-level action embeddings, and classifier-free guidance are established ingredients; the clearest new element is convolution initialization. Section 4.2 also characterizes cited approaches including DIAMOND and NWM as unsuitable for fine-grained online conditioning, despite subsequently evaluating them as autoregressive action-conditioned baselines. The positioning needs greater precision.

Some headline performance claims exceed the evidence. Table 1 acknowledges that robot baseline FID values use an incorrect evaluation implementation, yet Section 5.1 still claims superior FID without recomputing comparable scores. Robot autoregressive predictions also trail action-conditioned fine-tuning on SSIM, LPIPS, and PSNR. On navigation, NWM outperforms Vid2World on LPIPS and DreamSim. These results support meaningful but mixed improvements, rather than general state-of-the-art superiority.

Evidence for faithful interactive dynamics remains limited. Most evaluation measures visual similarity, while action branching is demonstrated qualitatively without quantitative counterfactual ground truth. Policy evaluation covers only one drawer-closing task, three checkpoints, and 50 simulated trajectories per checkpoint. Figure 5 predicts 26% success for the initial policy despite 0% reported real-world success. Missing confidence intervals, real-world evaluation details, and simulator comparisons prevent strong conclusions about reliable policy assessment.

The ablations do not sufficiently establish the proposed mechanisms' contribution to the large cross-domain gains. They cover only RT-1 at 30k steps, compared with 100k for the principal results, without reported variability. The action-guidance comparison changes both training-time dropout and inference-time guidance, leaving their effects entangled. Extrapolative transfer has mixed advantages over masking without guidance. Full-budget ablations across domains and a history-conditioned bidirectional diffusion baseline would better establish the benefits of architectural causalization.

Claims of generality, data efficiency, and practical scalability are insufficiently tested. All experiments use one pretrained backbone, with no reduced-data curves or controlled comparison isolating the contribution of pretraining. Sampling uses 50 DDIM steps with guidance, but inference latency and memory are unreported. Consequently, the quality-versus-cost tradeoff against the interactive baselines is unclear.

Appendix A.3 contains a proof gap: the intercept-error derivation bounds a sum of signed coefficients multiplying second derivatives evaluated at different points using the absolute value of the coefficient sum. This does not follow directly from the stated derivative bound and requires additional justification. The temporal smoothness assumption is also unvalidated for independently noised internal features. This does not establish failure of the implemented p=2 initialization, but weakens its claimed theoretical justification.
